summary: Intermittent route flap when corporate PAC not discovered on specific office Wi‑Fi VLANs causing VPN default-route drop
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-10 morning, a number of employees on the Floor-4 corporate Wi‑Fi SSID experienced short VPN disconnects and application failures. Symptoms were correlated with packets showing the client removing the default route after failing to locate the corporate proxy PAC (wpad/proxy.pac).

Impact:
- ~12 developers (floor-4) reported intermittent drops while working on remote repos and internal dashboards.
- Typical user impact: sudden 10–30s application failures, followed by VPN reconnect or manual re-auth.

Environment:
- SSID: Redwood-Corp-Employee-Floor4 (VLAN 204) via Aruba AP group floor-4-controller
- VPN client: OpenVPN-based corporate client v2.7.3 (configured for split-tunnel with proxy auto-detect requirement)
- PAC hosting: internal proxy service proxy.internal.redwood (behind nginx/reverse-proxy, served from us-west datacenter)
- DHCP: VLAN 204 uses DHCP relay to central server; DHCP option 252 expected for WPAD

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Join Redwood-Corp-Employee-Floor4 SSID.
2) Launch corporate VPN client (auto-connect policy enabled).
3) During PAC discovery, client attempts WPAD via DHCP option 252 then falls back to http://wpad.proxy.internal/wpad.dat.
4) When PAC lookup fails or times out, the VPN client removes/rewrites default route and triggers reconnect, resulting in application errors.

Observed behavior:
- Windows and macOS clients on that SSID fail PAC discovery ~15–40% of attempts.
- tcpdump from an impacted client shows DHCP OFFER without option 252 on the floor-4 subnet intermittently.
- Traceroutes from client to proxy.internal show intermittent ICMP timeout when routed via the AP controller's relay path.
- AP controller logs show SNAT to management IP for some relay requests.

Expected behavior:
- DHCP option 252 (WPAD) reliably delivered by DHCP relay; PAC file fetched; VPN keeps routes stable.

Logs and artifacts attached (referenced below):
- tcpdump snippets (client): wpad DHCP DISCOVER/OFFER without option 252 (see tcppcap-2026-03-10-floor4.log)
- AP controller relay logs: relay-logs-2026-03-10.txt
- VPN client debug logs from a consenting user: vpn-debug-ashley-2026-03-10.log
- nginx access/error logs for proxy.internal around event window

Temporary workaround used by impacted users:
- Manual set of proxy to http://proxy.internal:8080 in browser until reconnect stabilizes (not ideal).
- Moving to wired port on floor-4 eliminated the symptom (indicates wireless relay path-related).

Request:
- Investigate DHCP relay behavior on VLAN 204 and AP controller configuration for WPAD delivery.
- Confirm PAC server availability from the AP controller routing path and ensure no intermittent SNAT/ACL is blocking HTTP requests to wpad endpoint.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:42 - Aisha Patel: Ticket created after Slack thread in #internal-support. Collected initial tcpdumps from two affected macOS machines and one Windows VM.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Marcus Lee: Assigned. I will start by validating DHCP option 252 delivery and AP controller relay logs. Can the network team provide the AP controller logs for VLAN 204?
2026-03-10 11:20 - NetOps (Elena Gomez): Uploaded relay logs: relay-logs-2026-03-10.txt. Observed that some relay requests are being proxied via the controller's mgmt IP when CPU is high.

2026-03-10 12:02 - Marcus Lee: Correlated tcpdump with relay logs. When controller CPU spikes, DHCP relay path falls back and strips option 252 on the OFFER. Hypothesis: relay implementation bug under high load.

2026-03-10 13:45 - SRE (Omar Khan): Confirmed that proxy.internal returns 200 for wpad.dat from the datacenter. No errors on upstream. But nginx shows occasional 499 (client closed) when requests traverse AP controller.
2026-03-11 09:10 - Marcus Lee: Rolled a temporary AP controller config change to force direct DHCP relay (avoid CPU-heavy path) for VLAN 204. Asked NetOps to monitor.
2026-03-11 11:32 - Elena Gomez: After config change, clients on floor-4 reported a drop from ~30% failure to ~2% over 4 hours. Will schedule controller firmware upgrade to address long-term fix.

2026-03-12 08:15 - Marcus Lee: Coordinated a short window with NetOps to push controller firmware on a subset of APs (canary). No regressions observed. Will keep ticket open until full rollout and 48h stability window.
investigation_notes: Ran tcpdump on three affected clients. Observed DHCP OFFER sequences missing option 252 when AP controller showed CPU load >85%.
AP controller has a legacy DHCP-relay implementation with a known issue for large concurrent relays; vendor doc mentions option truncation under high load.
Confirmed PAC server reachable from core network; timeouts correlate with controller path where nginx logs 499.
Hypothesis: when PAC lookup times out, VPN client aborts proxy auto-detect and rewrites routes which triggers the observed application failures.
Tested forcing direct DHCP relay via a controller policy for VLAN 204 which reduced repro rate dramatically (from ~30% to ~2%).

Next step: schedule full controller firmware upgrade and audit DHCP relay configuration on other office VLANs to prevent recurrence. Also consider VPN client safeguard to avoid route removal if PAC not immediately found.
resolution: Mitigation applied: Temporary controller policy pushed to force direct DHCP relay for VLAN 204 which reduced incident rate to acceptable levels. Canaries for controller firmware upgrade completed without regressions. Long-term action items: full firmware rollout scheduled 2026-03-15, vendor bug submitted referencing relay implementation behavior, and a follow-up ER (Engineering Request) to add a VPN client option to tolerate transient PAC lookup failures. Monitoring set for 72 hours post-rollout.
next_steps: Complete full firmware rollout for AP controller across all floors (scheduled 2026-03-15).
Open engineering ticket to add VPN client resilience to PAC timeouts (ref: GH PR above).
Add synthetic PAC fetch monitor from AP controller path to alert on >5% failure in 15m window.
Document workaround in internal KB and notify floor-4 users of scheduled maintenance window.
